headline: A 2013 Senate bill would have funded the Transportation and Housing and Urban Development departments and some related agencies for fiscal year 2014, but the Senate did not advance it.
what_it_does: The bill would have provided fiscal year 2014 money for the Department of Transportation, the Department of Housing and Urban Development, and several smaller agencies. It included many detailed rules, such as limits on air traffic control costs, housing assistance eligibility, Amtrak overtime, and federal employee travel and conferences. The Senate refused to take it up or end debate on it, so none of these provisions took effect.

who_it_affects.group: Public housing residents and section 8 voucher holders
who_it_affects.how: The bill would have set new rent floors, required housing agencies to inspect units every two years instead of yearly, and changed income eligibility to use an extremely low-income standard.
The bill would have capped Amtrak overtime pay at $35,000 per employee unless the president of Amtrak waived the cap for safety reasons.
The bill would have changed how airports share costs for air traffic towers and set minimum federal grant amounts for certain airports.

who_it_affects.group: Students and young adults seeking section 8 housing aid
who_it_affects.how: The bill would have limited section 8 rental assistance for many unmarried students under age 24 who are not veterans, disabled, or have dependent children.

who_it_affects.group: Texas drivers and toll road users
who_it_affects.how: The bill would have barred new tolls on certain federally assisted highway segments in Texas that were not already tolled.

who_it_affects.group: Federal employees who travel or attend conferences
who_it_affects.how: The bill would have required reports on vehicle fleets and conference costs and limited the number of staff sent to certain international conferences.
